parsed.explanation: The dossier shows no criminalisation and a post-2015 equality reform, but gender identity is not stated as protected and no enforcement record exists. Trans-specific border, custody, facilities, care, violence and remedy evidence is absent; the only societal signal is dated 2015 LGBT stigma. A visitor outed faces low legal severity, but social and institutional treatment is unresolved. This sits above documented exclusion states and below jurisdictions with working protections: reduced-to-elevated boundary.

entry_documents.exposure: No trans-specific border rule, marker check, or screening practice is documented; dossier only advises carrying documents matching the passport used for entry.
entry_documents.protection: No documented visitor-facing protection; absence of a marker-change procedure is resident-facing and not shown to reach visitors.
entry_documents.interaction: Open question whether a document/presentation mismatch would trigger scrutiny; no subnational interaction documented.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: No criminalisation of same-sex conduct and no trans-specific offence documented; no police detention or custody practice reported.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: No documented protocol on custody placement, legal aid, or consular access for trans visitors.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Without a trans offence, detention risk is not shown; if detained for another reason, placement is undocumented.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Dossier records one national legal position and no subnational variation; no facility-access, ward, or bathroom rule documented.
federal_state_facilities.protection: No documented inclusive facilities rule or enforcement.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: No local/national interaction is evidenced because no subnational content exists.

care_services.exposure: No trans-specific care denial, medication seizure, or hospital-placement rule documented.
care_services.protection: No documented care-access protection or complaint route for trans visitors.
care_services.interaction: Unknown whether ordinary care would expose identity; no facility or insurance interaction documented.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: No state threat-framing or trans-specific enforcement documented; 2015 report notes societal stigma toward LGBT people, dated and not applied through law.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: 2018 constitutional equality covers sexual orientation; gender identity enumeration and enforcement are not stated.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Equality guarantee lacks documented complaint mechanism, so practical reach for trans visitors is unresolved.

minors_guardians.exposure: No age-specific rule, school, shelter, or guardian disclosure risk for trans minors is documented.
minors_guardians.protection: No documented protection or remedy for travelling minors or guardians.
minors_guardians.interaction: No documented interaction with border, care, or facility rules.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No trans-specific violence data or police-response record is documented; only dated 2015 societal stigma.
street_violence_police_response.protection: No hate-crime or police-response protection specific to gender identity documented.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Cannot assess whether police protect or worsen trans visitor victimisation.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Equality guarantee has no recorded complaint body, tribunal decision, or enforcement action; legal gender recognition is absent but resident-facing.
remedies_unknowns.protection: No operative remedy for trans visitors is documented.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Open questions about document treatment and service denial cannot be resolved from the record.

anchor_checks.comparison: Higher: no documented entry bar, visitor register, or routine exclusion of trans travellers. The dossier lacks any recorded administrative exclusion or police stop pattern comparable to 0.35-A.
Higher: no documented secondary screening, refused admission, or humiliating border practice. Unlike 0.55-B, border exposure is an open question rather than a recorded practice.
Lower: 0.75-C documents trained border officers, tribunal appeals, and brief detention with remedies; here no trans-specific protection, complaint body, or enforcement record is documented.

parsed.synthesis: The combined regime is a single national system with no documented subnational variation. Legal criminalisation is absent, and the 2018 equality reform is a positive climate signal, but it is framed around sexual orientation and lacks any documented enforcement route. The only negative social evidence is dated 2015 stigma. Trans-specific border, custody, facility, care, violence, and remedy evidence is absent, so the visitor faces low legal severity if outed but unresolved social and institutional treatment. This supports a reduced-to-elevated score, above exclusion regimes and below jurisdictions with documented working protections.
